title: We believe in the Lord of all the worlds.
subtitle: The magicians name the One above every throne
then: The magicians fell in prostration and proclaimed their belief in the Lord of all that exists. Ibn Kathir reports from Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazzah that {reward}they did not raise their heads before being shown Paradise and the Fire{/reward}. In front of the man who claimed to be their lord, they named a greater one.
now: You have worked for years to please one person: a parent, a boss, an audience. Their approval was your whole world. Then one day you see it clearly. {idea}They are one small part of a world Allah owns.{/idea} The weight shifts off your chest.
old: The person I answer to most is the biggest power in my life.
new: Allah is Lord of all the worlds, including everyone I fear or try to please.
try: In your next prayer, slow down at Rabbil alamin and think of the one person whose approval you chase.

title: The Lord of Musa and Harun, they made it unmistakable.
subtitle: Being specific so no one could twist their words

row.title: Lord of Musa and Harun
sub: the One these two called to

then: Fir'awn called himself lord of his people. So the magicians did not leave room for doubt: {idea}they believed in the Lord of Musa and Harun{/idea}. Ibn Ishaq reports they said that had Musa been a magician, he could not have beaten them.
now: At a family dinner someone mocks people who pray. You could mumble something about everyone believing in something. Or you could say, gently, {idea}I pray, and it matters to me.{/idea} Clarity is a kind of courage.
old: It is safer to keep my faith vague in public.
new: Real belief is willing to say whose side it is on.
try: Once this week, when your faith comes up, say plainly and kindly what you believe.

title: You believed before I gave you permission?
subtitle: A tyrant who wants to license even belief
then: Fir'awn accused the magicians of a plot with Musa. Ibn Kathir says Fir'awn knew it was false: Musa had never met them. He said it to {trap}deceive the ignorant masses{/trap}, citing 43:54: he fooled his people, and they obeyed him.
now: You quietly start praying again, and someone at home says: who told you to do that? Since when do you decide things without asking? {trap}Some people want a say even over your heart.{/trap} Your faith does not need their sign-off.
old: I need the approval of the people around me before I change.
new: No one has the right to give or withhold permission for my belief.
try: Think of one good change you are waiting for permission to make. Make a small start on it today.

title: When the argument was lost, he reached for threats.
subtitle: Cruelty is what is left when proof runs out
then: Fir'awn threatened the magicians with severe mutilation and crucifixion. Ibn Kathir reports from Ibn 'Abbas that {trap}Fir'awn was the first to use these punishments{/trap}. He had lost the debate in front of everyone, so he turned to force.
now: In an argument you are losing, you feel the urge to raise your voice, bring up an old mistake, threaten to leave. {trap}That urge is the sign you have run out of reasons.{/trap} {idea}Notice it, and stop.{/idea}
old: If I cannot win the point, I can at least make them afraid.
new: Turning to threats is the clearest sign I have lost the argument.
try: Next time you feel like threatening or shouting, say: I need a minute. Then step away.

title: To our Lord we are returning, so do what you will.
subtitle: Remembering the return made the threat small
then: The magicians answered calmly that they were returning to their Lord. Ibn Kathir explains they meant: {idea}Allah's judgment is greater than yours{/idea}, so we will be patient with your punishment today. In 20:72 they told him: you can only decide for the life of this world.
now: Your manager threatens to block your promotion unless you sign off on numbers you know are false. Your stomach drops. Then you remember: {reward}one day I meet Allah, not this manager.{/reward} The threat is still real, but it gets smaller.
old: The person threatening me holds my future.
new: I am returning to Allah, and that puts every other threat in its place.
try: When something frightens you today, say quietly: inna ila rabbina munqalibun. Then breathe.

title: Our Lord, pour patience on us and let us die Muslim.
subtitle: The first prayer of new believers under threat

row.title: patience and a good end
sub: hold me firm to the last

then: The magicians told Fir'awn his only grievance was that they believed when the signs came. Then they prayed for patience and to die as Muslims. {reward}They started the day as sorcerers and ended it as martyrs{/reward}, as Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and others said.
now: A long illness, a hard marriage, a debt that will take years. You keep praying: take it away. Some days the better prayer is: {reward}pour patience on me, and let me end well.{/reward}
old: Faith means asking Allah to remove every hardship.
new: Sometimes the bravest prayer is for patience to carry it and a good end.
try: Add this to your dua today: Rabbana afrigh alayna sabran wa tawaffana muslimin.

title: The oppressors called the oppressed the mischief-makers.
subtitle: Fir'awn's chiefs push him to crush Bani Isra'il
then: The chiefs asked Fir'awn if he would let Musa and his people spread mischief. Ibn Kathir says: {trap}amazingly, they were worried Musa would cause mischief, when they were the mischief-makers{/trap}. Fir'awn renewed his order to kill the boys, and Ibn Kathir notes the opposite of what he intended came to pass.
now: At home, you are the one who slams doors, but you call your teenager the troublemaker when they finally push back. {trap}It is easy to name others as the problem.{/trap} {idea}Look first at who started the harm.{/idea}
old: The ones who disrupt my order are the problem.
new: Sometimes the order I am defending is the real corruption.
try: Think of someone you call difficult. Ask honestly what part of it you caused.

title: Seek help in Allah, be patient: the earth is His.
subtitle: Musa's advice to a frightened people
then: Fir'awn had just renewed his threat. Musa did not promise an easy road. He told his people to {idea}seek help in Allah and be patient{/idea}, because the earth belongs to Allah and {reward}the good end is for the righteous{/reward}.
now: Your landlord raises the rent again. The company is cutting jobs. It feels like other people own every piece of your life. {idea}The earth is Allah's.{/idea} Ask Him for help, do the next right thing, and wait well.
old: Whoever controls the ground controls my outcome.
new: The earth belongs to Allah, and the end belongs to those who fear Him.
try: Before you face something stressful today, make one short dua for help first, then act.

title: Harmed before you came, and harmed since you came.
subtitle: Tired believers, and the test that comes after relief

row.title: relief is a test
sub: He will see how you act

then: The Children of Israel told Musa they had suffered before he came and still suffered after. Musa answered that perhaps Allah would destroy their enemy and make them successors, {idea}so He may see how you act{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says he was encouraging them to be grateful when hardship is replaced by blessing.
now: For years you prayed for a stable job. Now you have it, the salary arrives every month. {idea}The question has changed.{/idea} It is no longer will Allah help me, but what am I doing with what He gave?
old: Once my problems are solved, the test is over.
new: Ease is its own test: Allah watches what I do with it.
try: Pick one blessing you prayed for in the past. Do one thing with it today that you would be glad Allah saw.

title: Hard years were sent so they might remember.
subtitle: Drought and shrinking harvests as a reminder
then: Allah tested Fir'awn's people with years of drought and poor harvests. Ibn Kathir reports from Raja' bin Haywah that {trap}a date palm would produce only one date{/trap}. The purpose is named in the verse: {idea}that they might remember{/idea}.
now: Business slows. The car breaks down the same week the boiler does. You curse your luck and scroll for distraction. {idea}A hard season can be an invitation{/idea} to stop and ask what Allah wants you to notice.
old: Hard times are just bad luck I have to get through.
new: Hardship can be a mercy meant to make me remember Allah.
try: Name one current difficulty. Ask: what is this reminding me of? Write one line.

title: Good times were ours; bad times were someone's fault.
subtitle: Taking credit for blessings, blaming others for trials

row.title: good season
sub: this is ours, we deserve it

row.title: good is mine, bad is yours

then: When good came, Fir'awn's people said it was theirs by right. When hardship came, they called Musa and his followers a bad omen. Ibn 'Abbas explained: {idea}their afflictions are with and from Allah{/idea}, but most of them did not know.
now: Your team hits the target: that was my strategy. The next quarter drops: the new hire slowed us down. {trap}Credit for me, blame for them.{/trap} The same pattern runs in families and marriages.
old: When things go well it is me, when they go badly it is someone else.
new: Both the good and the hard come from Allah, so I thank Him and look at myself.
try: Next time something goes wrong, before naming anyone, ask: what was my part?

title: Whatever sign you bring, we will not believe.
subtitle: A mind closed before the evidence arrives
then: Fir'awn's people told Musa that whatever sign he brought, they would call it sorcery and never believe. Ibn Kathir describes this as {trap}rebellion, defiance of the truth, and insistence on falsehood{/trap}. They closed the door before anyone knocked.
now: You have already decided your sister-in-law is selfish. She brings food when you are sick and you think: she just wants to look good. {trap}No act can reach you once the verdict is in.{/trap}
old: I have already made up my mind about this.
new: A heart that decides in advance cannot see any sign at all.
try: Pick one person you have a fixed opinion about. Look for one good thing they did this week.

title: Five clear signs, one after another, and still arrogance.
subtitle: Flood, locusts, lice, frogs, blood
then: Allah sent the flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood as distinct signs. Sa'id bin Jubayr describes how {idea}each one was removed when Musa prayed{/idea}, and each time they broke their promise. {trap}They remained arrogant{/trap}, a people set on wrongdoing.
now: The first warning from your doctor. Then the second. Then the test results. Each time you promise to change, and each time the fear fades and you go back. {idea}Every sign was also a door held open.{/idea}
old: One more warning and then I will change.
new: Every sign I ignore was a mercy that gave me another chance.
try: Name one warning you have had more than once. Take one concrete step on it today.

title: Remove this and we will believe, they promised every time.
subtitle: Promises made under pressure

row.title: a deal with Allah
sub: help me and I will change

then: When each punishment struck, they came to Musa: pray to your Lord, and if He removes this, we will believe and let the Children of Israel go. Ibn Ishaq describes the same {trap}promise made again and again{/trap} with each new sign.
now: In the hospital corridor waiting for news, you promise: if they are okay, I will pray every day. They recover. Two weeks later the prayer mat is folded away. {idea}A promise made in fear needs to be kept in ease.{/idea}
old: If Allah gets me out of this, then I will change.
new: The test of a promise made in hardship is what I do after relief.
try: Remember one promise you made to Allah in a hard moment. Do one part of it today.
